issues.item: Triggers: Family-Related Comments: Comments on family
issues.explanation: For an assault trauma, 'comments on family' is not impossible as a trigger, but paired with the rest of the profile it lacks a clear assault-linked context. The other triggers and memory items point to sensory/intrusive re-experiencing, whereas this item suggests a family-related theme not represented elsewhere in threat, appraisals, or memory.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Grief Reminders: Anything that reminds me of someone I have lost
issues.explanation: 'Avoid grief reminders' implies a bereavement/loss-focused coping target, but no other selected items indicate death loss or grief as a central aspect of the assault trauma. This maladaptive strategy does not fit the rest of the profile, which centers on assault-related intrusive memory, dissociation, and social avoidance.

vignette: As a school counselor for over three decades, 68-year-old Thomas had spent his career helping students navigate life's challenges. Yet, in the past year, he found himself increasingly struggling to manage his own emotions. The traumatic event that set this downward spiral in motion occurred when Thomas was violently assaulted by an unknown assailant while walking home from a late-night school meeting. He vividly recalled the smell of antiseptic wafting through the air as he lay on the hospital floor, his head throbbing with pain. That night's events had become seared into Thomas' memory like snapshots in his mind - disjointed moments frozen in time: the sound of footsteps behind him, the sudden impact, and the eerie silence that followed. Even now, whenever memories of that fateful evening resurfaced, Thomas was consumed by the same terror he felt at the time. Sudden fragments would flash before his eyes without warning - an image of his broken glasses, a glimpse of the assailant's face - only to vanish as quickly, leaving him shaken. The assault had also left Thomas with an intense aversion to certain smells, particularly hospital or antiseptic scents. Even brief whiffs of these odors would transport him back to that nightmarish evening in the emergency room, sending his anxiety soaring. His loved ones began noticing a change in Thomas after this incident - he became withdrawn and increasingly hesitant to engage with others, especially if it meant being emotionally close. Thomas was also troubled by another trigger: the smell of alcohol. His assailant had reeked of cheap liquor that night, and now even passing a pub or walking past someone sipping a beer would bring back unwelcome memories. To cope, Thomas developed deliberate dissociation strategies - he would mentally leave his body or 'blank out' when confronted with these triggers. He tried to convince himself that if he could just 'numb out,' the emotions wouldn't catch up. As time passed, Thomas started avoiding social gatherings and one-on-one interactions, opting instead for solitary pursuits like reading or gardening. His job as a school counselor became more challenging; he found it increasingly difficult to connect with his students on an emotional level, leading him to question his own effectiveness in the role. Even conversations with his wife began to feel suffocating, prompting Thomas to pull away from intimate moments. This gradual withdrawal took its toll on Thomas' relationships and overall well-being. His marriage grew strained as his wife struggled to understand why her usually affectionate partner had become so distant. As a school counselor, Thomas noticed that his lack of emotional engagement with students resulted in decreased trust - kids stopped opening up about their problems, sensing his unease. It wasn't until he began experiencing vivid flashbacks during sessions with students, however, that Thomas realized the gravity of his situation. A recent episode where he 'zoned out' mid-conversation had shaken him; the concerned look on a student's face still lingered in his mind. The fear that he might be failing both himself and those around him pushed Thomas to finally seek help. With a heavy heart, Thomas scheduled an appointment with a clinical psychologist, hoping to find ways to re-engage with life without being overwhelmed by the memories of that fateful night. His greatest fear now was losing his connection with loved ones forever - and he clung to the hope that therapy could guide him toward healing and rediscovery.
